column1: # Every moment Claude Code offers a harness, and Felix's stance on each.
# This file exists because two coverage gaps were found by a person noticing.
# The Stop hook checked the gate and never asked anyone to verify their claims;
# SubagentStop was not wired at all, so a subagent could finish, report success,
# and be believed. Both are the same defect — a completion moment with nothing
# at it — and neither was findable by reading the code, because absence has no
# line number.
# A stance is required for every event. `wired` must be backed by an entry in
# hooks.json, and `declined` must carry a reason someone can argue with. An
# event with neither is the gap, and `felix coverage` fails on it.
# `holds` is what keeps a decline honest. `wired` is re-checked against reality
# every run; `declined` never was, so a reason could stop being true and no
# check could tell. The column names a literal that must still appear in
# hooks.json for the reason to stand — PreCompact is declined *because* the
# SessionStart matcher says `compact`, so narrowing that matcher turns this row
# red instead of leaving a stale excuse in place. `-` means the reason rests on
# judgement rather than on anything readable; that is allowed and counted, not
# failed, because forcing a literal out of every row would only invent fake ones.
# The point is not the current answers. It is that a new event added by the
# platform, or a hook quietly removed, cannot sit here unnoticed.
# event
SessionStart
column3: bind the session and record the moment in lifecycle.log, a resume included and silently; mount doctrine, tidy, report what is due

column1: UserPromptSubmit
column3: route the work, name the tool due next, mount matching lessons

column1: PreToolUse
column3: refuse what this project has forbidden, on the shell and on the files a session reaches for

column1: PostToolUse
column3: record what was reached for, so what is never used can be found

column1: Stop
column3: refuse completion on an unverified tree, then ask for verification of the claims

column1: SubagentStop
column3: a subagent finishing is a completion moment too, and the parent inherits its report

column1: SessionEnd
column3: roll the session's tool calls into the ledger, with zeroes for what went untouched

column1: PreCompact
column3: SessionStart matches on compact, so doctrine is re-mounted afterwards; nothing needs saving before

column1: Notification
column3: fires when Claude wants attention. Felix has nothing to add, and speaking here would break stealth in the middle

column1: SubagentStart
column3: a subagent starts blank; give it the project, the constitution and the gate that will judge it

column1: PostToolBatch
column3: PostToolUse already records every call the ledger needs, and recording the same work twice would double every count

column1: PostToolUseFailure
column3: a tool that failed has already reported so to the session, and Felix would add nothing by repeating it. Bound here by another plugin the day it was installed; whether the ledger undercounts reaches that failed is the open question, and that decides whether this becomes wired
